findings.claim: The per-level maze CELL MAP is SCENARIO.DBS bank 2, record `levelId` (the starting level = zone 0 = record 0), read VERBATIM by the same bank reader that loads the floor/ceiling images. record = SCENARIO.DBS[ base[2] + levelId*recsize[2] .. +recsize[2] ], base[2]=37896 (0x9408, from DISK.HDR), recsize[2]=1346 (from MASTER.HDR). The 1346-byte record is the in-RAM maze block at DGROUP *0x4faa. NO decompression — the live *0x4faa bytes [0 .. 1345] are byte-identical to scenario.dbs[37896 .. 39241]. (The diff only begins at record byte 1346 = the start of the NEXT bank-2 record; every MazeBlock plane ends well before that: highest plane offset = pit end 0x49a = 1178 < 1346.)

evidence.details: find() of the live maze-block head64 (00 01 01 00 01 01 02 03 ...), the gxBase table (120 128 120 128 120 128 10 18 10 18 26 26), the gyBase table (116 116 124 124 132 132 10 10 18 18 10 18), the +0x60 N plane and the +0x120 W plane ALL land at scenario.dbs offset 37896 + their MazeBlock sub-offset (head64 @37896, N @37896+0x60, W @37896+0x120, gxBase @37896+0x1e0, gyBase @37896+0x1ec). 37896 == base[2] (DISK.HDR u32 @ (2+1)*4) and (37896-base[2])/recsize[2] = 0, so it is bank 2 record 0. Live *0x4faa[0..1345] vs scenario.dbs[37896..39241]: 0 diffs (first diff at byte 1346, the next record). bank 2 holds 16 records ((59432-37896)/1346=16); records 2..13 are the floor IMAGES for zones 0..11 (maze-asset-loader.json), so the maze-DEFINITION records are 0/1 (rec0 != rec1, 599 byte diffs — distinct, not duplicates).

findings.claim: Within the 1346-byte record, the MazeBlock fields are at the offsets the classify findings pinned (maze-classify-projection.json / maze-classify-gating.json): gxBase = +0x1e0 (12 bytes), gyBase = +0x1ec (12 bytes); and FIVE contiguous MSB-first bit-planes indexed by cell = region*64 + cellA*8 + cellB (12 regions × 64 cells = 768): N = +0x60 (2 bits/cell), W = +0x120 (2 bits), special4 = +0x1f8 (4 bits), orient2 = +0x378 (2 bits), pit = +0x43a (1 bit). Decoding these planes from the on-disk record reproduces the live MazeBlock exactly. cellA is the ×8 axis, cellB the ×1 axis; the region resolver (wmaze 0x357a/0x35b7) maps a global (gx,gy) to (region, cellA, cellB) via gxBase[r] <= gx <= gxBase[r]+7 AND gyBase[r] <= gy <= gyBase[r]+7.
